abstract: QUERCETIN REVERSES TPA INHIBITION OF GAP JUNCTIONAL INTERCELLULAR COMMUNICATION IN RAT GLIAL CELLS
affiliation: Dept. of Pediatrics and Human Development, Michigan State U., E. Lansing, MI, 48824
summary: The naturally occurring bioflavonoid quercetin reversed the TPA inhibition of gap junctional intercellular communication in rat glial cells. Fluorescent recovery after photobleaching (FRAP) analysis and a scrape loading/dye transfer assay demonstrated quercetin to reverse the TPA action in a dose and time dependent manner. Quercetin may reverse TPA inhibition of gap junctional intercellular communication by preventing TPA activation of protein kinase C. Quercetin can be used as a model compound to investigate the action of TPA-like chemicals on gap junction function in neural cells.
